title: Setting Up My Preferred Settings
intro: Before a single note goes down, get the program out of your way. These are the settings worth checking on a fresh install, and each one says exactly where it lives.

tips.t: Run two buffer sizes, not one
tips.d: Open Settings with ⌘, and go to Audio > Devices. Keep the I/O Buffer Size small while you track so monitoring latency stays low. Raise it when you mix: a larger buffer lowers the load on your Mac's CPU. A buffer too small for your Mac shows up as clicks, pops and crackles.

src.label: Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Overview of Logic Pro settings

tips.t: Set Processing Threads to Automatic
tips.d: In Settings > Audio > Devices, Processing Threads is set to Automatic by default, and Apple recommends leaving it there. The one exception Apple names: set a thread count yourself when you run other CPU-intensive apps at the same time as Logic.

src.label: Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Choose the right Multithreading mode
tips.d: In Settings > Audio > Devices, the Multithreading pop-up offers two modes. Playback Tracks is the older behaviour: when several audio tracks record, or a Track Stack is selected for live input, all the input DSP runs on one thread and one core. Playback & Live Tracks spreads that load across threads but adds slightly more overall load. Use it only if you have demanding live tracks.

src.label: Apple — About the Multithreading setting in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set Process Buffer Range to Large to avoid overloads
tips.d: In Settings > Audio > Devices, Process Buffer Range sets the buffer Logic uses to compute mixes and effects. It is separate from the I/O buffer and offers Small, Medium and Large. Apple's advice for avoiding system overloads is to set it to Large.

src.label: Apple — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Uncheck Software Monitoring if you monitor through your interface
tips.d: If your audio interface supports hardware (direct) monitoring, turn off Software Monitoring in Settings > Audio > General. With it on, your input is processed in software and some latency is unavoidable. Apple's advice is to switch it off whenever you listen through your interface or mixing console.

src.label: Apple — General Audio settings in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — General Audio settings in Logic Pro for Mac (IS locale)

tips.t: Turn on Allow Quick Punch-In
tips.d: Choose Record > Allow Quick Punch-In, or Control-click the Record button in the control bar and choose Allow Quick Punch-In. With it on, you can punch in and out of recording on the fly while the project keeps playing.

src.label: Why Logic Pro Rules — Never Lose An Audio Take Again With Quick Punch-In
Why Logic Pro Rules — #16 Autopunch, Quick Punch-In, & Replace Recording Modes
Apple — Punch in and out of audio recordings in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Make the bar and the beat click sound different
tips.d: In the project settings, the Metronome pane controls the audio click, which comes from Klopfgeist, a virtual metronome sound source on the Click channel strip. Separate Note and Velocity fields set the note number and velocity of the notes generated for the bar, group, beat or division, so you can make the bar and the beat sound different. The Tone slider changes the sound from a short click to a pitched percussion sound like a wood block or claves. The Audio Click checkbox also works with any other plug-in you load on the Click channel strip.

src.label: Apple — Metronome project settings in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Klopfgeist in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn on scrubbing with audio in the Tracks area
tips.d: Settings > Audio > Editing > “Scrubbing with audio in Tracks area”. With it on, you can scrub audio regions in the Tracks area with the Scissors or Solo tool and find a spot by ear. Maximum Scrub Speed and Scrub Response fine-tune how it feels.

src.label: Apple — Audio Editing settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Leave the MIDI Reset Messages at their defaults
tips.d: Leave Logic's Reset Messages settings alone. Apple says Logic handles MIDI reset messages automatically and intelligently, so you can keep the defaults. The Control 123 (All Notes Off) and Control 121 (Reset Controls) options exist for compatibility with older MIDI devices. Switch one on only if an older synth needs it.

src.label: Apple — Reset Messages settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Fix doubled notes from a controller
tips.d: If notes double when you record from a keyboard synth, turn Local Off on the synth. If your keyboard has no Local Off setting, use Project Settings > MIDI > General > “Instrument Without MIDI Thru Function” and choose that instrument there. When a track assigned to it is selected, Logic does not pass your controller's MIDI through, which avoids the doubled notes.

src.label: Apple — General MIDI project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn on Enable Complete Features first
tips.d: Go to Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced and select Enable Complete Features. It is one checkbox. Leave it off and advanced features stay hidden, including project alternatives and backups, beat mapping, and expanded mixing and automation.

src.label: Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Colour regions individually, not by track
tips.d: Choose Logic Pro > Settings > View, click Tracks, and set the Region Color pop-up to Individual instead of As Track Color. With Individual you can colour regions independently of their track, so you can colour-code by part. With As Track Color you cannot colour regions individually.

src.label: Apple — Tracks View settings in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Color regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn on “Show help tags”
tips.d: In Logic Pro > Settings > View > General, select Show help tags. While you edit, help tags show the function name, the region or event name or number, the position and parameter values.

src.label: Apple — General View settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set Auto Set Locators to By Region Selection
tips.d: Control-click the Cycle button in the control bar, click Auto Set Locators and choose By Region Selection. The locators and the cycle area are then set to the borders of the selected region.

src.label: Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac
macProVideo — 6 Logic Pro X Cycling Tips

tips.t: Turn on “Limit Dragging to One Direction” in the Tracks area
tips.d: Tick the "Limit Dragging to One Direction: In Tracks" checkbox in Logic Pro > Settings > General > Editing. Once you start a drag left or right, movement locks to the horizontal axis, so you cannot nudge a perfectly placed region onto another track by accident. To actually change tracks, let go, reselect, and drag up or down — or hold Shift to override the limit for one move. There is a matching checkbox for the Piano Roll and Score.

src.label: Apple — Move regions in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Read the Clean Up list before you confirm it
tips.d: File > Project Management > Clean Up always asks first and shows exactly what it will remove. Read the list — it deletes whole unused audio files, not just unused portions of them.

src.label: Apple — Clean up projects in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set your sample rate before you record, not after
tips.d: Choose File > Project Settings > Audio and set the Sample Rate before you record or import anything. If an audio file's sample rate does not match the project's, it plays back at a different pitch. To have incoming files matched to the project rate, select "Convert audio file sample rate when importing" in File > Project Settings > Assets.

src.label: Apple — Set the sample rate of a project in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set the recording bit depth in Settings > Recording
tips.d: Recording bit depth is set in Logic Pro > Settings > Recording. Match it to your audio device's bit depth. With 32-bit float, files are about 33% larger than 24-bit, but you can remove clipping just by lowering the region's gain.

src.label: Apple — Recording settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn on Smart Tempo “Keep Project Tempo” by default
tips.d: In File > Project Settings > Smart Tempo, set the project tempo mode to Keep Project Tempo. In Keep mode Logic Pro maintains the project tempo when you record or import audio. Adapt Project Tempo changes the project tempo to match a recording or imported file, so use it only temporarily.

src.label: Apple — Choose the project tempo mode in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Stop new recordings arriving pre-quantised
tips.d: With no region selected, the Region inspector shows "Default Settings", and those values are applied to newly recorded regions. If new takes arrive quantised, check the Quantize value there and set it to off. Capture the performance first; quantise as a decision.

src.label: Apple — Use the Region inspector in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit, not re-retrieved)

tips.t: Check Tuning when a synth sounds subtly off
tips.d: Project Settings > Tuning sets the tuning for Logic's included software instruments. If a synth sounds subtly wrong against a sample, check here first: Equal Tempered turns off any alternative tuning, and the Tune slider should read A 440 Hz unless you meant to change it.

src.label: Apple — Tuning project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Copy your assets into the project so it travels
tips.d: In File > Project Settings > Assets, select the copy checkboxes, such as "Copy audio files into project". The files are copied in the next time you save. From then on you can move or copy the project without losing any file references.

src.label: Apple — Manage project assets in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Save a Session Start template and set it as the default
tips.d: Build one project with your usual tracks, buses, reverb and marker colours, then choose File > Save As Template. Then, in Project Handling settings, set the Startup Action pop-up to "Create New Project Using Default Template" and use the Default Template button to choose your template.

src.label: Apple — Project Handling settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Save your starting channel strip as a setting
tips.d: Build one channel strip the way you always start: your go-to EQ, compressor and sends. Click the Setting button at the top of the strip, choose "Save Channel Strip Setting as", pick a folder, name it and click Save. On any new track, load it from the Setting button's pop-up menu or from the Library.

src.label: Apple — Work with channel strip settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Give each colour a fixed meaning
tips.d: Press ⌥C to open the Color palette (or Control-click a region and choose Name and Color > Show/Hide Colors), then click a colour. Decide once what each colour means to you (drums, vocals, keys, reference) and colour your template that way, so every project opens with the same language.

src.label: Apple — Color regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Make a Project Alternative before big changes
tips.d: File > Project Alternatives > New Alternative gives you another version of the project: name it and click Done. Make one before every big arrangement change. Alternatives need Enable Complete Features in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced. File > Project Alternatives > Edit Alternatives lets you rename or delete them; you can't remove the Main alternative.

src.label: Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Hit ⌘S often: every save banks a backup
tips.d: Each time you save with File > Save (⌘S), Logic keeps a backup of the current project alternative, up to ten per alternative. To go back, choose File > Revert to and pick one; they're listed newest first. Backups need Enable Complete Features. Build the reflex of hitting ⌘S every time you finish a thought.

src.label: Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Move the Sound Library to an external drive on purpose
tips.d: Logic Pro > Sound Library > Relocate Sound Library moves the library off your system drive: pick the drive or volume and click Relocate. Afterwards, don't rename that drive, or Logic Pro won't be able to find the Sound Library.

src.label: Apple Support - Relocate the Sound Library (from prior audit, not re-retrieved)

tips.t: Save the project as a Package so it travels
tips.d: In the File > Save As dialog, choose "Organize my project as: Package" to save the project as a single file (package) containing its assets. Assets saved in the project are still there when you move or copy it. Choose Folder instead if you want a project folder with subfolders for each asset type.

src.label: Apple — Save Logic Pro for Mac projects
